title: Go-Live Runway and Week-3 Stability Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the technical and operational runways for an enterprise customer go-live and the stabilization activities leading up to the end of week three post-cutover. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Solutions Engineering, SRE, and the customer's technical stakeholders. The goal is to ensure predictable availability, cost controls, and measurable quality during the high-risk window immediately after go-live.

Scope

- Applies to Dedicated and Private deployment modes and hosted customers with enterprise SLAs.
- Covers pre-go-live readiness, day-of execution, and week-1 through week-3 stabilization.
- Excludes long-term feature rollouts (see related roadmap/feature-release pages).

Quick summary of ownership

- CSE (Primary runbook owner): coordinates customer comms, activation gating, and weekly status.
- SRE: infra monitoring, incident response, capacity adjustments.
- Solutions Engineering: test harness, integration verification, and debug.
- Customer Engineering Lead: on-site or designated technical contact for approvals.

Pre-Go-Live (T minus 14 to T minus 1 days) — readiness gate checklist

1) Technical validation (owners: SolutionsEng, CustomerEng)
   a) End-to-end smoke test passes using production-like traffic profile (see test matrix).
   b) Authentication and network connectivity validated (IDs, firewall rules, VPC peering).
   c) Model variant pinning and fallback policy confirmed.

2) Capacity & performance (owners: SRE, InfraOps)
   - Reserved capacity validated for peak QPS; target headroom >= 30%.
   - Batching and KV cache configuration reviewed against expected median sequence length.
   - Latency SLO target listed: p95 <= 250ms for single-token probes; p99 <= 800ms.

3) Cost controls and quotas (owners: Finance, CSE)
   - Per-route quota set for first 72 hours: default 50% of expected peak to avoid runaway costs.
   - Alerting on daily cost burn rate > 150% of forecast.

4) Observability & alerting (owners: SRE, Observability)
   - Traces, metrics, logs are routed to central stack; sampling rules verified.
   - Key dashboards created: tokens/day, tokens/second, error-rate, avg-latency-by-model.

Pre-Go-Live checklist table (copy/paste to customer kickoff)

| Area | Criteria | Owner | Pass/Fail |
|------|---------|-------|----------|
| Network | VPC peering, IP allowlists configured | InfraOps | ____ |
| Auth | API key exchange and rotation verified | CustomerEng | ____ |
| Runtime | Model pin and fallback configured | SolutionsEng | ____ |
| Observability | Dashboards live + alerting enabled | SRE | ____ |
| Billing | Quotas + budget alerts set | Finance/CSE | ____ |

Day-of Go-Live — hour-by-hour run of show (owners annotated)

- T-2h: Final smoke tests (SolutionsEng) — run 3 synthetic scenarios at production rate.
- T-1h: Enable throttling and quotas; confirm monitoring ingestion (SRE).
- T-15m: Stakeholder sync in #cust-<customer>-go-live Slack channel (CSE).
- T+0: Switch traffic per agreed plan (blue/green or DNS cutover) (InfraOps + CustomerEng).
- T+15m: Run quick sanity probes (latency, error-rate, 10 sample user sessions) (SolutionsEng).
- T+60m: First-hour stabilization review — share dashboards and any rate anomalies (All).

Immediate post-go-live checks (first 72 hours)

- Checkpoint cadence: 15m, 1h, 4h, 12h, 24h, then every 24h until day 7.
- Probing script (run as CI job or adhoc):
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-infer","input":"healthcheck prompt"}' | jq '.status, .latency'
- What to watch: sudden jump in token generation time, p50->p95 increase > 3x, rising error-rate > 1%.

Week 1 stabilization (days 1–7)

- Focus: eliminate recurring errors, tune batching and cache settings, tighten cost controls.
- Tasks:
  - SRE: Set adaptive sampling for traces to capture errors at p99.
  - SolutionsEng: Increase KV cache TTL for repeated prefixes if cache-miss ratio > 40%.
  - CSE: Run a QBR-style health call on day 3 with customer technical leadership.

Week 2 stabilization (days 8–14)

- Focus: performance tuning, model quality checks, and rollback readiness.
- Tasks:
  - Run model quality spot checks against customer prompt set (10–50 prompts).
  - Revisit autoscaling policies — target concurrency headroom and warm-up thresholds.
  - Finance: Convert provisional quotas to target production quotas where safe.

Week 3 stability & final handback (days 15–21)

- Focus: operational handback to BAU and reduced monitoring cadence. Criteria to move to BAU:
  1) Error-rate <= 0.3% for 7 consecutive days.
  2) Latency SLOs met p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 800ms for 7 consecutive days.
  3) Cost variance <= +/- 20% of forecast for 7 consecutive days.
  4) No active escalations in last 72 hours.

- If all criteria met, schedule BAU transition meeting and update owners to default rotations.

Escalation matrix and rapid contacts (use in incident communication)

- Level 1 (Customer-facing): CSE on-call — Slack: @cse-primary, Email: cse-primary@redwood.ai, PagerDuty: PD-1234.
- Level 2 (SRE / Infra): SRE on-call — Slack: #sre-oncall, PagerDuty: PD-2001.
- Level 3 (Engineering / Runtime): Runtime eng lead — PagerDuty: PD-3004, Phone: +1-415-555-0167.

Escalation steps (numbered)

1) Triage in Slack channel and attach initial triage template (incident type, impact, first seen).
2) If impact > P1 (complete customer outage) escalate to Level 2 within 10 minutes.
3) For persistent degradation beyond 30 minutes, call Level 3 and create incident bridge.

Sample incident triage template to paste into channel:

---
Incident type: (outage / degraded / cost-anomaly)
First observed: (timestamp UTC)
Impacted routes/models: (list)
Customer impact: (all traffic / subset / background jobs)
Current mitigation attempted: (quarantine model / reduce QPS / fallback variant)
Next actions: (owner + ETA)
---

Operational playbook snippets

1) Temporarily reduce model concurrency via admin API:
  curl -X POST https://console.redwood.example/api/admin/limit 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_KEY>' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"customer_id":"cust-1234","model":"rwd-3b-infer","concurrency_limit":10}'

2) Enable fallback to smaller model variant (for graceful degradation):
  PATCH /v1/customers/cust-1234/policies
  {"fallback_policy":"rwd-1b-infer"}

Telemetry and queries (examples you can run)

- PromQL: error-rate across customer routes (1m):
  sum(rate(redwood_requests_failed_total{customer="cust-1234"}[1m])) / sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{customer="cust-1234"}[1m]))

- SQL (usage billing table):
  SELECT day, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cost) as cost
  FROM billing.usage
  WHERE customer_id='cust-1234'
  GROUP BY day ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 14;

- Synthetic probe example (k6 script snippet):
  import http from 'k6/http';
  export default function () {
    const res = http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-3b-infer',input:'healthcheck'}), {headers:{Authorization:'Bearer ${__ENV.API_KEY}', 'Content-Type':'application/json'}});
    check(res, {'status is 200': (r) => r.status === 200});
  }

Rollback plan (when to trigger and steps)

- Trigger criteria:
  - Unrecoverable p99 latency > 2x target for 2 hours and mitigation fails.
  - Persistent error-rate > 5% for 1 hour despite scaling and throttling.
  - Regressions in model quality affecting customer’s business metrics.

- Rollback steps (owners annotated):
  1) Notify stakeholders and open an incident bridge (CSE).
  2) Switch traffic to previous deployment (InfraOps) using blue/green or model pin rollback.
  3) Verify successful rollback via synthetic probes (SolutionsEng).
  4) Perform postmortem and remediation plan within 72 hours (SRE + SolutionsEng).

Release sign-off (checklist before BAU handoff)

- All pre-go-live checklist items are green.
- No P1/P0 incidents in the last 72 hours.
- Customer acceptance test signed by Customer Engineering Lead.
- Finance confirms quotas and billing alerts are in place.

Postmortem and learning capture

- For any incident with customer impact greater than 1 hour or cost > $5k unexpected, open a postmortem in the incident channel and publish within 7 business days. Include root cause, timeline, action items, and owner for each action.

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands and config snippets

- Check active model variants for customer:
  GET /v1/customers/cust-1234/config

- Example model cache config YAML:
  cache:
    enabled: true
    ttl_seconds: 3600
    max_keys: 250000

- Typical autoscaler min/max for dedicated pool (example):
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 12
  target_utilization: 0.7

FAQ

Q: How long should we keep quotas conservative after go-live?
A: Conservative quotas are recommended for the first 72 hours. If metrics are stable, move to target quotas in week 2.

Q: Can we change model variants after go-live?
A: Yes, but treat model changes as a deployment. Validate in staging or use canary rollouts.
